front: Ideal gas equation and its SI units?
back: pV = nRT: p in Pa, V in m³, n in mol, R = 8.31 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, T in K.

front: Mr of a gas or volatile liquid?
Assumptions of the kinetic theory of an ideal gas?
back: Random rapid motion; negligible molecular volume; no intermolecular forces; perfectly elastic collisions.
Molecules colliding with the walls of the container (force per unit area).

front: When do real gases behave most ideally?
Why do real gases deviate at high pressure and low temperature?
back: Molecular volume is no longer negligible and intermolecular attractions become significant.
cm³ × 10⁻⁶ = m³; dm³ × 10⁻³ = m³; kPa × 10³ = Pa; °C + 273 = K.

front: Which gases deviate most from ideal behaviour?
back: Those with strong intermolecular forces, e.g. NH₃ (hydrogen bonding), SO₂ (polar); He is the most ideal.
